name: backend_engineer_python_v1
_comment: Labelled evaluation set for the scorer comparison. Labels are 0-5 human
relevance grades (5 = fast-track, 0 = irrelevant), assigned as a recruiter
hiring a mid/senior Python backend engineer would assign them.
The set is built to expose the failure mode of keyword matching, not just
to be easy. Three candidates are deliberate traps:
c08  senior Java/Spring engineer - hits java, api, sql, docker, aws in the
legacy keyword list and so scores high, but is the wrong stack (label 2)
c05  Node.js developer - hits node, api, rest, sql, docker (label 3)
c10  QA tester - mentions python, sql, api and so scores non-trivially
on substring matching despite being unsuitable (label 1)
Conversely c13 (Python data engineer) and c04 (Python/Flask) are strong,
transferable candidates whose value a literal Django keyword match misses.
Replace this synthetic set with real, recruiter-labelled applicants as soon
as a campaign has produced them - synthetic data validates the pipeline, it

responsibilities: Design and build REST APIs for a high-traffic product
Model and optimise relational data access
Review code and mentor junior engineers
job.raw_jd: We are hiring a Backend Engineer (Python) with 3-7 years of experience to design and build REST APIs for a high-traffic product. You will own service reliability, model relational data on PostgreSQL, containerise services with Docker, and write automated tests. Required: strong Python, Django, REST API design, PostgreSQL, Docker, unit testing. Nice to have: AWS, Celery, Redis, Kubernetes, CI/CD.

candidates.notes: 7y senior Python/Django, payments scale, strong quantified impact.
4y solid Django/DRF, right in the experience band, less depth at scale.
Python data engineer with real FastAPI service work - strong transferable fit.
5y Python/Flask, strong API design, Django only peripheral.
Right stack exactly, but 2y - under the band and shallow.
Heavy Python scripting and platform depth, but not a product backend dev.
TRAP: hits many legacy keywords. Real backend skill, wrong language.
TRAP: senior and keyword-rich (java/api/sql/docker/aws) but no Python.

Competent frontend engineer, no backend ownership.
TRAP: mentions python, sql, api, selenium - substring-friendly, unsuitable.
Enterprise sales manager - entirely different field.
